answer: The direct cause of the Challenger accident was a combustion gas leak and the failure of the pressure seal in the right Solid Rocket Motor aft field joint. This leak initiated at or shortly after ignition, weakened and/or penetrated the External Tank, and initiated vehicle structural breakup. The seal failure itself was attributed to a faulty design unacceptably sensitive to temperature, physical dimensions, material characteristics, reusability effects, processing, and the reaction of the joint to dynamic loading.
ground_truth: Failure of the primary and secondary O-ring seals in the right SRB aft field joint allowed combustion gases to escape and impinge on the External Tank.

Consequently, a warm O-ring follows the opening of the tang-to-clevis gap, whereas a cold O-ring may not. ground_truth: Cold temperatures increased Viton rubber hardness and delayed seal resiliency, preventing proper sealing of the joint during ignition pressure.
